turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. I came in today because... well, I keep hearing Garrett's voice. It's as clear as if he's standing right behind me, like when I'm out on the trail or just sitting in my painting room. 

I mean, logically, part of me knows he's dead. But in the moment it happens, it feels completely real to me. So, I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.

turns.doctor_question: When you hear Garrett's voice, do you believe he's actually there speaking to you, or do you know it's something your mind is creating?
turns.patient_response:
Well, like I was just saying, it really depends on the exact moment. Right when I hear him, I completely believe he's there. The voice is so clear that I'll actually turn around expecting to see him standing right behind me. 

It's only after a minute or two that the rational part of my brain catches up. That's when I remember that he's gone, so it has to be my mind making it up. But in that split second when it happens? No, I don't think it's my imagination at all. It feels entirely real to me.

I had never heard him like that before this shift happened. I mean, I've grieved him, of course, but this wasn't like ordinary grief. It only started when my mood got really sped up like that.
